title: U.S. House · Georgia's 7th Congressional District
area: Northeast suburbs of Atlanta, including Gwinnett and Forsyth counties.

context.text: Incumbent Rich McCormick (R) previously represented the old 6th District (2023-2025) before running in and winning this redrawn 7th District seat in 2024; he advanced unopposed from the Republican primary. Tony Kozycki won the June 16, 2026 Democratic primary runoff over Case Norton after a four-way May 19 primary.

candidates.name: Rich McCormick
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Georgia's 7th Congressional District (since 2025; previously represented Georgia's 6th District 2023-2025)

summary.text: Rich McCormick is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Georgia's 7th Congressional District, previously representing Georgia's 6th District from 2023 to 2025 before running in the redrawn 7th District in 2024. He is an emergency medicine physician and former Marine Corps and Navy officer.

background.text: Lives in Suwanee, Georgia; served in the U.S. Marine Corps and U.S. Navy; earned an M.B.A. from National University and an M.D. from Morehouse School of Medicine.
Worked as an emergency medicine physician with Gwinnett Medical Center and Northside Hospital, a Marine officer instructor with Georgia Tech and Morehouse College, and a pilot.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (chair of the Investigations and Oversight Subcommittee; Space and Aeronautics Subcommittee), the House Committee on Armed Services (Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation; Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees), and the Committee on Foreign Affairs in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Tony Kozycki
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 16, 2026 Democratic primary runoff over Case Norton after a four-way May 19 primary.

summary.text: Tony Kozycki is a former Navy fighter pilot and immigration attorney, and the Democratic nominee for Georgia's 7th Congressional District. He says he decided to run after Rich McCormick refused to help with the case of a Georgia Army veteran facing deportation without a hearing before an immigration judge.

background.text: Grew up in LaGrange, Georgia; graduated from the United States Naval Academy in 2008 and earned a law degree from Georgia State University College of Law in 2021.
Served in the U.S. Navy from 2004 to 2017 as a fighter pilot, completing three combat deployments in Iraq, Afghanistan, and Syria, and later worked as an immigration and criminal defense attorney.

priorities.text: Says he will fight to ban congressional stock trading, require blind trusts, and strengthen ethics laws, criticizing McCormick for staying silent on government corruption despite sitting on the Oversight Committee.
Says the district needs immigration reform that restores due process and ends abusive enforcement practices, drawing on his work as an immigration attorney.
Says he will work to lower the cost of living for working families, including expanding the child tax credit, investing in affordable housing, and raising the minimum wage.

positions.summary: Says the immigration system needs reform to restore due process and end what he calls abusive enforcement practices, citing his work representing families and a detained veteran.
Says he will work to raise the minimum wage as part of lowering the cost of living for working families.
